$comment: Machine-readable module list for llama-cpp-integrations' integration layer. Read by the PKGBUILD (to know what to apply) and by anyone regenerating a patch. One module = one concern; a conflict in one must never block the others.

modules.name: server-model-hooks
modules.applies_to: llama.cpp v0.4.0 (and later — touches stable C++ interfaces)
modules.purpose: Expose pinned remote models to the router: model listing, per-model proxy targets, and the tool listing the panel tabs read.

modules.name: panel-shell
modules.applies_to: NOT YET EXTRACTED — see README, 'Which llama.cpp version this targets'
modules.purpose: The Vite alias (@mcp-panel -> panel/frontend) and the single render line that mount the whole panel. Without these two edits nothing in panel/frontend is reachable.

modules.name: compaction
modules.purpose: Summarize a long conversation with the model, keep the summary as a new message, and trim what is resent. Nothing is ever deleted. Includes the zero-context-size fix: a remote model reports n_ctx 0, and treating that as a real budget made one API call per message.

modules.name: media
modules.purpose: Make images work for models that cannot see: the image is attached for its preview, saved to disk by the panel backend, and only its path is sent to a text-only model (a vision MCP tool reads it from there).

modules.name: markdown
modules.purpose: Rendered output: enhanced code blocks and their styling.

modules.name: rag-pages
modules.purpose: Routes that surface the RAG collection browser and editor (the pages themselves live in panel/frontend, reached through the @mcp-panel alias).

modules.name: slash-commands
modules.purpose: Register the panel's commands in the WebUI's own / picker (it ships three; this adds the rest) and provide panel-command-runtime.ts, the panel's single import surface for anything from node_modules.

modules.name: permission-modes
modules.purpose: Permission mode per chat rather than per browser, and a gate that asks for anything that can modify state: the always-allow list may only silence tools that cannot write, EDIT_APPROVED_TOOLS is empty, and the default mode is manual.

modules.name: incognito
modules.purpose: A chat that is never written to disk: every write for it is intercepted at DatabaseService (the single choke point) and served from memory, plus the localStorage stream-resume write is skipped.

modules.name: tailwind-source
modules.purpose: @source for panel/frontend. Tailwind generates a class only if it is found in a scanned file, so without this the panel renders unstyled — the dashboard's grid collapsed to one column and its colours vanished.

notes.why_not_all_extracted: The live tree (master-era UI) and the packaged tree (v0.4.0) are different UI generations, so a patch extracted from one does not apply to the other. Modules marked NOT YET EXTRACTED exist and work in the live tree; their patch files still have to be generated against whichever tree a given build uses.
notes.archive: archive/ holds the original v0.4.0-targeted panel-constants.patch and panel-ui.patch. They do not apply to the live tree and are kept as history only.
notes.apply_order: server-model-hooks is independent of the UI modules. The UI modules must be applied in the order listed only if two of them touch the same file — currently none do, which is the property this split is meant to preserve.
